text: This month, a machine we built gets so far away that light needs a whole day to reach it.
It's Voyager 1. It left Earth in 1977.
It has been flying for almost fifty years, at about seventeen kilometres every second.
On November eighteenth, it passes twenty-five point nine billion kilometres. One light-day.
If we say hello, it hears us a day later. Its answer takes another day to come back.
Its radio is about as strong as a fridge light bulb, and our giant dishes still catch it.
Most of its instruments are switched off now, to save its last bit of power.
On board is a golden record, with music and greetings from Earth, in case anyone ever finds it.
But here's the thing. The nearest star isn't one light-day away.
It's more than fifteen hundred. At this speed, Voyager would need over seventy thousand years to cross that gap.
